title: Koszul wedge cycles present the exterior conormal
statement: For a commutative ring A, ideal I and degree n, let S be the concrete type of all finite tuples g in I, vectors v for a degree-n Koszul wedge and quotient-tensored Koszul cycles z with iCycles(z)=wedge(v) tensor 1. The A-linear map from S ->0 A to the exterior conormal [new-r4-conormal-exterior-module] sending each generator to the wedge of the conormal classes of the g-linear combinations of v is surjective.

source.place: Koszul complex after quotient base change; exterior-power universal property

proof.text: The contraction formula for the Koszul differential [lem-weil-pbc-koszul-differential] expresses the boundary of a wedge as a sum of wedges multiplied by linear combinations of the tuple elements. Each coefficient lies in I, so tensoring with A/I kills all differentials.

Lift each vector of a conormal wedge to I using toCotangent_surjective; take the tuple of these lifts and its standard basis wedge. The inverse of iCyclesIso supplies an actual cycle, whose generator evaluates to the original conormal wedge.

Use exteriorPower.iotaMulti_span and Submodule.span_induction. The zero and sum cases are linearity. In the scalar case lift a coefficient in A/I to A by quotient surjectivity and multiply the preimage by that lift.
